Definition: from G3844 and G1525; to come in alongside, i.e. supervene additionally or steathily:--come in privily, enter.
BiblicalUsage: Pareiserchomai means to come in alongside, to enter privily. Paul uses it in Galatians 2:4 of the false brethren who came in privily, and in Romans 5:20, where the law entered, that the offence might abound, so that where sin abounded, grace did much more abound.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that two things entered alongside in these verses, false brethren and the law, and the outcomes could not be more different: one brought bondage, the other made room for grace to abound all the more.
